items.title: [@sveltejs/kit] SvelteKit : XSS via untrusted cache-control header in prerendered page
items.summary: ImpactApplications that prerender pages and use setHeaders to set a cache-control header from an untrusted source are vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS).SvelteKit inserts the header value into a <meta http-equiv="cache-control"> tag without escaping it. An attacker who can influence this value at prerender time can break out of the content attribute and inject HTML or JavaScript into the generated page. The injected code can then execute when users visit the page.PatchesThe fix escapes the header value before inserting it into the generated HTML. Upgrade to @sveltejs/kit version 3.0.0 or later.WorkaroundsAvoid forwarding untrusted cache-control header values with setHeaders on prerendered pages. Use a fixed, trusted cache policy instead.Referenceshttps://github.com/sveltejs/kit/security/advisories/GHSA-27mw-82g8-phjjhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-114061https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/commit/d9d55b579743c80ee7cb59c272d864fd9253dae7https://github.com/sveltejs/kit/releases/tag/@sveltejs/kit@3.0.0https://www.vulncheck.com/advisories/sveltekit-before-3.0.0-xss-via-cache-control-header-in-prerendered-pageshttps://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27mw-82g8-phjj

items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc: Memory-lifecycle tools overwrite unowned notes or partially commit lifecycle changes
items.summary: Summarycreate_entity, link_entities, rename_entity, unlink_entities and delete_entity regenerate a memory note's body from SQLite at the computed memory/<type>/<name>.md path. When a note already existed at that path and was not owned by the entity being written (a hand-authored note, or an orphan left by a different entity whose name sanitized to the same path), its entire body was overwritten on the next write naming that (type, name), keeping only its frontmatter. Separately, several of these tools inserted or removed their SQLite row before the fallible filesystem step, so a refused note write could leave a relation gone, a retired status committed, or the wrong entity deleted.Detailscreate_entity and link_entities inserted the SQL row or relation before materialization.rename_entity seeded the destination path with a direct atomic write that bypassed the ownership check, and for a status-only rename could commit a retired status with the note write refused.unlink_entities removed the relation row before discovering the source note's rematerialization would be refused.delete_entity's cascade could delete the target and its relations before a neighbour's note was found to be foreign.The overwrite exists in every released version since materializeEntity shipped (git show v1.0.1:packages/server/src/memory/materialize.ts).ImpactAn authorized caller with memory-write scope (any agent using the M5 memory tools) can, without intending to, destroy the body of a vault note outside the entity it is writing, and can leave the memory graph inconsistent with the notes on disk. Snapshots-before-write (restore_note) mitigate the overwrite only where snapshots are enabled and the note had been written through obsidian-tc before.PatchesFixed in 1.31.4 at the shared primitive: materializeEntity refuses to write over a note whose obsidian_tc_id is missing or belongs to another entity; a new assertNoteOwnership pre-check runs before any SQLite mutation in the three lifecycle tools, so a refusal is a no-op; create_entity and link_entities roll back the row they had inserted. Verified by test/m5-memory-ownership.test.ts, which covers all five call sites and the rollback.WorkaroundsNone that preserve the tools. Disabling the write:memory scope for callers prevents the write path entirely.CreditFound by the maintainer while building obsidian-tc memory import (PR #978); the vulnerability class was independently confirmed by a cross-vendor adversarial review.ReferencesPR #978 (fix and test), CHANGELOG ## [1.31.4] ### Securitypackages/server/src/memory/materialize.ts, packages/server/src/tools/m5/memory-lifecycle-tools.tsReferenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-r3g7-r4hr-m258https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-115478https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/978https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/99f7914ca0fbeed92e7c4d39cc8c3e5830dab133https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/blob/v1.31.4/CHANGELOG.mdhttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.31.4https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r3g7-r4hr-m258

items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc HTTP transport lacks Origin/DNS-rebinding protection, enabling drive-by vault access on loopback
items.summary: ImpactThe Streamable HTTP transport was constructed without enableDnsRebindingProtection/allowedHosts/allowedOrigins and performed no Origin-header validation. With the documented auth.mode: "none" loopback default, a drive-by web page could POST http://127.0.0.1/mcp and receive caller http-local with scopes ["*"] — full vault read/write — via DNS rebinding / a forged Origin.PatchesFixed in 1.3.1. Upgrade to >= 1.3.1. The transport now enables DNS-rebinding protection and allowed hosts/origins and returns HTTP 403 on an invalid Origin (per MCP 2025-11-25).WorkaroundsDo not expose the HTTP transport with auth.mode: "none"; require JWT auth, or bind to a non-loopback interface behind a proxy that validates Origin.Referenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-pqh8-4pj7-32xxhttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/74https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/6428bfe6fdfd43aa7b4b369be3aecd6a268fb928https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.3.1https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-77363https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pqh8-4pj7-32xx

items.title: [obsidian-tc] obsidian-tc Bridge tools leak denied-note data via unfiltered sibling fields
items.summary: ImpactBridge tool results filtered only the items array against the read ACL and passed sibling fields through unfiltered: tasks_filter emitted groups whose counts reflected denied notes, makemd_query returned ...result siblings, and list_templates enumerated Templater template paths and parsed user-function bodies with no read-whitelist gate. A caller could infer or read data from notes outside its read ACL.PatchesFixed in 1.3.1. Upgrade to >= 1.3.1. All path-attributable fields are now scrubbed or fail-closed, and list_templates is gated on the read whitelist.WorkaroundsDisable the affected bridge tools (tasks_filter, makemd_query, list_templates) via tool visibility.Referenceshttps://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/security/advisories/GHSA-43r2-c7g8-prc8https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-77362https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/pull/75https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/commit/5ab2109274acf0070601fa71a62b14ddc9652309https://github.com/The-40-Thieves/obsidian-tc/releases/tag/v1.3.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-43r2-c7g8-prc8
